meta.title: SceneShift
meta.description: SceneShift turns HDR on while your movie player or game is open, and puts the display back when it closes.
hero.title: HDR when you need it, back to normal when you're done
hero.text: SceneShift switches HDR on or off for the apps you choose. Open your movie player and the display turns HDR on. Close it and the display goes back to how it was.
hero.store: Coming soon to the Microsoft Store
steps.title: How it works
steps.1.title: Pick an app
steps.1.text: Choose from the apps you have open, or browse for any .exe file.
steps.2.title: Pick a display
steps.2.text: Click the display on a map laid out like your desk, and choose HDR on or off.
steps.3.title: Use the app as usual
steps.3.text: SceneShift changes the display when the app opens and puts it back when it closes.
guide.title: Guide
guide.rules.title: The rules page
guide.rules.text: Right now shows what each display is doing. Below it, each app you set up has a card with its status, a switch to turn the rule off, and a menu to edit or delete it.
guide.rules.status: Active: the app is open and its rule is in effect.
Waiting: the rule is ready and the app is not open.
Off: you switched the rule off. It stays saved.
Paused: every rule is paused from the tray or the window.
Display not connected: the rule starts working again once that display is back.
guide.add.title: Adding an app
guide.add.text: Select Add app, pick the app, then the display and what HDR should do. Each app has one rule, so picking an app that already has one opens that rule instead.
guide.tray.title: The tray icon
guide.tray.text: Click the icon to see each display, switch HDR by hand, pause every rule, or open SceneShift. Right-click it for a short menu with Restore all displays now and Exit.
guide.restore.title: Putting displays back
guide.restore.text: SceneShift remembers how each display was before it changed it. When the app closes, the display goes back to that, so HDR you turned on yourself stays on. If the PC restarts or SceneShift closes unexpectedly, the displays are put back the next time it starts.
guide.settings.title: Settings
guide.settings.text: Start with Windows, animations, accent color and language. You can also restore every display from here.
help.title: Help

help.items.question: The HDR choice is greyed out
help.items.answer: Windows reports that this display doesn't support HDR. Check Settings > System > Display > HDR in Windows. If HDR can't be turned on there, SceneShift can't turn it on either.

help.items.question: My app isn't in the list
help.items.answer: The first tab shows apps with a window open. Open the app first, look in the All apps tab, or use Browse for .exe.

help.items.question: A display stayed in HDR or SDR
help.items.answer: Open SceneShift and choose Restore all displays now in Settings, or from the tray menu.

help.items.question: HDR keeps switching on and off
help.items.answer: Another program may be switching HDR for the same app. Close it, or turn off its rule for that app.

help.items.question: Uninstalling
help.items.answer: Uninstall SceneShift from Start or Settings > Apps. Its settings are removed with it.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.text: Found a problem or have an idea? Open an issue on GitHub. English or Thai are both fine.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: SceneShift works entirely on your PC.
privacy.reads.title: What SceneShift reads
privacy.reads: Running apps: which programs are running and where their executable files are, to know when an app with a rule opens or closes. It does not read what those apps show or contain.
Displays: each display's name, size, refresh rate and HDR state, to show them and to switch HDR.
Installed apps: the apps in your Start menu, listed when you add a rule.
privacy.stores.title: What SceneShift stores
privacy.stores: Your rules and settings, the display state it needs to put your displays back, and a small log of errors, in SceneShift's own folder on your PC. Uninstalling the app removes them.
privacy.sends.title: What SceneShift sends
privacy.sends: Nothing. SceneShift does not connect to the internet, has no telemetry, and shares no data with anyone.
privacy.contact.title: Contact
privacy.contact: For questions about this policy, open an issue on GitHub.
